knowledge_point.title: Sketching the Solution Curves of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3 \left(x - 2\right)^{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3 \left(x - 2\right)^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =3\int \left(x - 2\right)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\left(\frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{3}}{3}\right)+C \\ y & =\left(x - 2\right)^{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

![](images/0a/0a2609542e1b48653ea5d167bb34d62f8b4ddefe3412b2a3c8804b7b50284fab.png)

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{e^{- \frac{x}{4}}}{8}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{e^{- \frac{x}{4}}}{8})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\frac{1}{8}\int e^{- \frac{x}{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\left(- 4 e^{- \frac{x}{4}}\right)+C \\ y & =- \frac{e^{- \frac{x}{4}}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

![](images/25/258e0e2dea305737216c1a4cbc8f448d93055b1c97eb8b8e73805b7fb8425c73.png)
